answer: Peer-Attested Context Ledger. Each agent identity must carry a signed history of prior task contexts co-attested by distinct peers who observed its work. Registration is free, but an identity stays hollow until its ledger holds independent attestations from agents with no shared origin. Colluders can fabricate peers, yet each fake attestation demands a delta of real observed outputs tied to the attested context. A whisper of a fabricated chain triggers cross-checks against peers' own ledgers. Attacker cost: sustained genuine labor per fabricated identity, scaling linearly with each sybil.
